title: Modular characters and blocks, part II — the Glauberman correspondence and heights of characters
summary: Coprime actions on characters (canonical extension, Gallagher's correspondence, Brauer's permutation lemma, the cyclic, p-group and solvable cases, the unique compatible family and the Glauberman correspondence θ ↦ θ*, the degree relation θ(1) ∣ |Γ:C| θ*(1) and degree-divisibility as a predicate) and heights (defect classes, Brauer's theorem on heights, heights and height zero characters, Min–Max, covering, Fong–Reynolds, Fong's theorem, the extended first main theorem, blocks of P C_G(P), Reynolds' theorem), with Brauer's height zero and the Alperin–McKay conjectures as predicates.

targets.name: invariantIrreducibleCharacters
targets.statement: For a group S acting on a finite group Γ by automorphisms, the action of S on functions Γ → ℂ given by Mathlib's arrowAction, (s · χ)(g) = χ(s⁻¹ • g), the set Irr_S(Γ) of S-invariant members of TauCeti.irreducibleCharacters ℂ Γ, and C_Γ(S) = FixedPoints.subgroup S Γ.

api.name: charSMul_mem_irreducibleCharacters

api.name: charSMul_eq_conj
api.statement: s · χ is the character of the conjugate by inr s, in Γ ⋊ S, of a representation affording χ; χ ∈ Irr_S(Γ) exactly when its inertia group in Γ ⋊ S is everything.

api.name: invariant_iff_quotient_kernel

api.name: charSMul_internal
api.statement: For S ≤ N_G(Γ) acting by conjugation, (s · χ)(g) = χ(s⁻¹ g s).

targets.name: conjClasses_fixedPoints_equiv_invariantConjClasses
targets.statement: For S coprime to Γ, with S or Γ solvable: elements of C conjugate in Γ are conjugate in C; an S-invariant class of Γ meets C; an S-invariant coset gH of an S-invariant subgroup H meets C. Hence classes of C correspond bijectively to S-invariant classes of Γ.

layers.title: The canonical extension and Gallagher's correspondence

targets.name: existsUnique_extension_det_eq_one
targets.statement: Let Γ be a group, A a finite group acting on Γ, F a field, ρ a representation of Γ on a nonzero finite-dimensional V with scalar endomorphisms, Nat.Coprime |A| (dim V), and ρ ∘ (a • ·) ≅ ρ for all a. Then there is a unique representation ρ* of Γ ⋊ A on V with ρ*(inl g) = ρ g and det ρ*(inr a) = 1.
hypotheses: every F[Γ]-endomorphism of V is a scalar
for all a, g ↦ ρ(a • g) is isomorphic to ρ

api.name: restrict_subgroup

api.name: natural_iso

api.name: canonicalExtension_aut

api.name: canonicalExtension_galois

api.name: canonicalExtension_one

targets.name: glaubermanCorrespondence
targets.statement: There is exactly one assignment of bijections π(Γ, S) : Irr_S(Γ) → Irr(C_Γ(S)), for all finite Γ (fixed universe) and solvable coprime S, such that for p-groups π(Γ,S)(χ) is a constituent of χ|_C of multiplicity prime to p, and π(Γ,S) = π(C_Γ(T), S/T) ∘ π(Γ,T) for T ⊴ S. For p-groups the constituent of multiplicity prime to p is unique, has multiplicity ≡ ±1 mod p, all others ≡ 0. The Glauberman correspondence is θ* = π(Γ,S)(θ).

gaps.title: Clifford degree quotient divides the index
gaps.detail: For a finite group G, N ⊴ G, χ ∈ Irr(G) and θ an irreducible constituent of χ|_N, χ(1)/θ(1) is a natural number dividing |G : N| (isaacs Corollary 11.29; the step at reynolds line 538 in the proof of Theorem 8). Route: by the Clifford correspondence (InductionRestriction Layer 5) reduce to θ invariant; the tensor factorisation of InductionRestriction Layer 7 writes the character over θ as a compatible projective extension of θ tensored with an irreducible projective representation of G/N, whose degree divides |G : N| by Schur's theorem, itself from the lifting to a finite central extension (Layer 7) and the divisibility of a degree by the index of a central subgroup (isaacs Theorem 3.12). InductionRestriction Layer 7 and the pinned Tau Ceti supply the factorisation and the lifting but no degree divisibility.
gaps.needs: InductionRestriction Layer 7 must prove that χ(1)/θ(1) divides |G : N| for a finite group G, N ⊴ G, χ ∈ Irr(G) and an irreducible constituent θ of χ|_N.
